subject: AcmeHealth private VPC dataflow — follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: AcmeHealth private VPC dataflow — follow-up & next steps

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed next steps so we can align on the private/VPC deployment details: 

Key takeaways from today's call:
- You have regulated PHI workflows and prefer a VPC/private deployment (no hosted inference).
- Primary concerns: PII/PHI handling, data residency (US-only), audit/logging controls, and strict egress rules to prevent lateral exfiltration.
- You may have an on-prem air-gapped environment for some workloads (we discussed a hybrid option).

Open questions we promised to follow up on (please confirm or correct):
1) Data ingestion: Is all input data coming from your internal APIs inside the VPC, or do you have external third-party feeds that need controlled ingress?
2) Retention & deletion: What are your retention requirements for logs, model inputs, and inference outputs? (e.g., 30 days, 1 year, indefinite)
3) PII redaction: Do you require automatic client-side PII redaction before passing data to the inference service, or should Redwood provide a server-side redaction pipeline?
4) Logging scope: For auditability, do you need full request/response logs (including inputs/outputs) or metadata-only logs (request IDs, timestamps, model/latency)?
5) Networking constraints: Confirm that outbound internet egress is blocked by default — any approved external endpoints (e.g., your S3, internal artifact stores, or monitoring endpoints) we should allow?
6) On-prem constraints: For air-gapped nodes, do you allow a staging/upgrade path via removable media, or must all updates be done by your ops team?

Proposed next steps:
- Technical dataflow review with your infra/security + our infra engineers (proposed window: next week).
- Share Redwood's private deployment checklist and a sample network diagram (attached).
- We’ll prepare a proposed deployment model (VPC peering vs. private link vs. on-prem appliance) and a short security controls mapping (SOC2 controls, encryption, KMS/HSM options).

Can you confirm a 60-min slot next Tuesday 09/22 or Wednesday 09/23 for the dataflow review? Also please attach any internal network diagrams or SOC/compliance questions you already have.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: AcmeHealth private VPC dataflow — follow-up & next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few clarifications below: 

1) Data ingestion: Primary inputs are internal APIs inside our VPC. We do have a small set of partner feeds that land in a controlled S3 bucket in our us-east-1 account — those are pulled into the VPC via a strict ETL job.
2) Retention & deletion: For inference inputs and outputs we need 90-day retention for troubleshooting, then automatic deletion. For security logs we retain 1 year.
3) PII redaction: We prefer client-side redaction for any PHI before it leaves our boundary. We would consider server-side redaction only if the data never leaves our VPC and we have guarantees around no persistent storage.
4) Logging scope: Metadata-only logs to start (request IDs, model version, start/end timestamps, latency). For escalations we may need full request logs but behind an approval and stored in our egress-controlled S3.
5) Networking constraints: No outbound internet from the inference subnet. Approved endpoints currently: our internal artifact S3 (s3://acme-prod-artifacts), Datadog ingest endpoint via private link, and our internal KMS.
6) On-prem constraints: Our air-gapped data center requires signed media for updates; we can accommodate a removable-media upgrade path but would like a documented handoff process.

I attached our SOC2 questionnaire and a higher-level network diagram. Let's lock in Tue 09/22 14:00 ET if that works for your team.

—Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Infrastructure, AcmeHealth
samir.shah@acmehealth.com

Attachments: AcmeHealth_SOC2_Request.pdf, acme_network_highlevel.png

Subject: Re: AcmeHealth private VPC dataflow — follow-up & next steps

Samir — perfect, thanks for the clarity and the attachments. Confirming Tue 09/22 14:00 ET for a 60-minute technical dataflow review with our infra/security engineers.

What we'll bring to the call:
- Detailed deployment options and tradeoffs (VPC peering, PrivateLink, dedicated subnet in customer VPC, and on-prem appliance flow).
- Logging & retention patterns we support in Private (metadata-only by default, configurable retention, request-level logs store to customer-owned S3 when requested).
- PII/PHI handling patterns: recommendations for client-side redaction + server-side safe-mode when running fully inside customer VPC.
- Proposed runbook for air-gapped upgrades and signed-media process.

Pre-call ask: please share one example inference payload schema (anonymized) and confirm whether your security team requires encrypted-at-rest for ephemeral KV cache and model artifacts (we support both customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed keys).

I'll send a calendar invite and a short read-ahead doc this afternoon.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa — quick note from our security team after reviewing your checklist: 

- They prefer that Redwood does not persist inference inputs or outputs in any Redwood-managed storage. If request-level logs are enabled for debugging they must be written only to our customer-owned S3 and be encrypted with our KMS key.
- For KV cache (to speed up responses) they require it to be ephemeral in-memory only, and periodically flushed; no disk persistence.
- They asked whether Redwood supports mutual TLS between our VPC and the Redwood service endpoint (we saw mention of PrivateLink during the call).

Also, Samir confirmed the 09/22 14:00 ET call — looking forward to the runbook proposals.

Thanks,
Priya
